translationRepairs: wuchen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu — all men of Chen — were ordered to subdue the Zhao territories, while Deng Zong of Ruyin was sent to pacify the Commandery of Jiujiang.
Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu — all men of Chen — were ordered to subdue the Zhao territories, while Deng Zong of Ruyin was sent to pacify the Commandery of Jiujiang.
Chinese 武臣 is the personal name Wu Chen; idiomatic “wuchen” fuses and lowercases it, and “Wu Chen” restores the correct form without changing the rest of the sentence.
wuchen arrived at Handan and declared himself King of Zhao. Chen Yu was made Grand General, and Zhang Er and Zhao Sao became the Left and Right Chancellors.
Wu Chen arrived at Handan and declared himself King of Zhao. Chen Yu was made Grand General, and Zhang Er and Zhao Sao became the Left and Right Chancellors.
Chinese 武臣 again names Wu Chen at Handan; correcting the fused lowercase “wuchen” to “Wu Chen” matches the source while leaving the self-declaration and appointments intact.
The King of Chen was furious. He seized the families of wuchen and his associates, intending to put them to death.
The King of Chen was furious. He seized the families of Wu Chen and his associates, intending to put them to death.
Chinese 武臣等家室 refers to Wu Chen and his associates’ households; “Wu Chen” is the required English name form for 武臣.

The King of Chen then sent envoys to congratulate Zhao. He moved the detained families of wuchen and the others into the palace, enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu, and urged the Zhao forces to hasten west into the passes.

The King of Chen then sent envoys to congratulate Zhao. He moved the detained families of Wu Chen and the others into the palace, enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu, and urged the Zhao forces to hasten west into the passes.
Chinese 武臣等家屬 again names Wu Chen among those whose families were moved; normalizing “wuchen” to “Wu Chen” is required and otherwise leaves the sentence accurate.
wuxu of Zhi had stationed troops at Xu. Zhang Han attacked and defeated them as well, and wuxu's entire force scattered and fled back to Chen.
Wu Xu of Zhi had stationed troops at Xu. Zhang Han attacked and defeated them as well, and Wu Xu's entire force scattered and fled back to Chen.
Chinese 伍徐 is the personal name Wu Xu; idiomatic “wuxu” wrongly fuses and lowercases both occurrences, and “Wu Xu” restores the correct form.
After defeating wuxu, Zhang Han attacked Chen itself. The Supreme Pillar of State, the Lord of Fang, was killed.
After defeating Wu Xu, Zhang Han attacked Chen itself. The Supreme Pillar of State, the Lord of Fang, was killed.
Chinese 伍徐 is again Wu Xu in the defeat notice; replacing fused “wuxu” with “Wu Xu” matches the source without altering the rest of the report.

When the Chen king was first established, Qin Jia of Ling, Dong Chen of Zhi, Zhu Jishi of Fuli, Zheng Bu of Qulu, Ding Ji of Xu and others all rose up specially. They led troops and surrounded Governor Qing of Donghai at Tan.

When the Chen king was first established, Qin Jia of Ling, Dong Xie of Zhi, Zhu Jishi of Fuli, Zheng Bu of Qulu, Ding Ji of Xu and others all rose up specially. They led troops and surrounded Governor Qing of Donghai at Tan.
Chinese 董緶 is Dong Xie (緶 = Xie), not “Dong Chen”; the proposed literal fix aligns with the Chinese and with the unit’s idiomatic “Dong Xie”.
Yongzhou's lands and Xiaohan's defenses were as before.'
Yongzhou's lands and Xiao and Hangu's defenses were as before.
Chinese 殽函 names the Xiao and Hangu defenses as two places; “Xiaohan” wrongly fuses them, and the trailing quote is not in the Chinese.
Chen She position, not noble than Qi, Chu, Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei, Song, Wei, Zhong Shan lords;
Chen She's position was not more exalted than the lords of Qi, Chu, Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei, Song, Wey, and Zhongshan;
Chinese lists 魏 then 衛 as distinct states, so the second English “Wei” must be “Wey”, and 中山 is Zhongshan; the proposed grammatical wording correctly distinguishes them.
His deep plans and far considerations, the way of marching and using troops, did not reach the scholars of former times.'
His deep plans and far considerations, the way of marching and using troops, did not reach the scholars of former times.
Chinese 深謀遠慮…非及鄉時之士也 has no closing quotation mark; the trailing apostrophe is scrape corruption and should be removed.
However, success and failure have different changes. Merit and enterprise are opposite.'
However, success and failure have different changes. Merit and enterprise are opposite.
Chinese 然而成敗異變，功業相反也 ends without a quote; deleting the stray trailing apostrophe restores the literal text.
Try to make the Shandong states measure length and compare greatness with Chen She, compare authority and measure strength, and they cannot be spoken of in the same year.'
Try to make the Shandong states measure length and compare greatness with Chen She, compare authority and measure strength, and they cannot be spoken of in the same year.
Chinese 則不可同年而語矣 has no closing quote; the trailing apostrophe is scrape corruption only.
However, Qin with its small lands,'
However, Qin with its small lands,
Chinese 然而秦以區區之地 has no quotation mark; removing the stray trailing apostrophe matches the source fragment.
achieved the authority of ten thousand chariots, suppressed the eight provinces and made the same rank come to court, for over a hundred years.'
achieved the authority of ten thousand chariots, suppressed the eight provinces and made the same rank come to court, for over a hundred years.
Chinese 百有餘年矣 closes the clause without a quote; the trailing apostrophe is scrape corruption and should be dropped.
Then took the six directions as home and Xiaohan as palace.'
Then took the six directions as home and Xiao and Hangu as palace.
Chinese 殽函 again names Xiao and Hangu separately, and the clause has no trailing quote; “Xiao and Hangu” plus removing the apostrophe restores both points.
